Covered high-level runway, success metrics (p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, uptime), net-new networking items for VPC/private deployment, and initial benchmark plan. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-28 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (CSM), Max (SE), Emily (Bayshore CTO), Raj (Lead ML), Sara (Product), Tom (DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining we're going to kick this off, psah sorry, start on time. i'm jordan from redwood, that's priya our csm and max se. quick round robin?
[00:17] Emily: hi all emily here, thanks. excited to get going.
[00:22] Raj: raj here, i'll own the ml integration and benchmarks.
[00:28] Sara: sara, product owner, mainly success criteria and ux.
[00:33] Tom: tom devops - networking / security questions.
[00:37] Priya: great, i'll outline the onboarding runway and key milestones.

[01:05] Jordan: high level — goal is pilot in 6 weeks, production in 12, but flexible. main success metrics you told us were p99 under 350ms for short prompts, cost target under $Y per 1k tokens, and zero data leakage. is that still right?
[01:27] Sara: yes those numbers still stand, product needs that latency for chat assist.
[01:34] Emily: and we need SOC2 artifacts and audit logs for compliance review.
[01:40] Jordan: totally, we'll include SOC2 attestation and audit log access in the docs.

[02:10] Max: from se perspective i'll propose a baseline plan: run a 1k prompt benchmark against your sample set, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost using hosted vs dedicated vs private configs. there may be trade offs — e.g. dedicated gives predictable throughput but costs more.
[02:33] Raj: can you run on our current model family? we use an open LLM fork, 34B style.
[02:38] Max: yes we can onboard that model, but we might recommend a quantized variant for cost. note: our runtime handles continuous batching and kv caching — although the transcript may call it 'kay v cache' — but it should reduce tokens for repeated contexts.
[02:55] Raj: kv cache oh got it, yep.

[03:20] Tom: networking: are we doing VPC peering or private deployment? we have strict egress rules so VPC peering preferred. Also need details on CIDR ranges and peering maintenance windows.
[03:35] Priya: we support VPC peering and on-prem private deployments. for peering we need your CIDRs, firewall owner contact, and proxy ports. We'll send a network diagram template.
[03:50] Tom: perfect. can we do a dry-run before pilot cutover?
[03:54] Max: yes, we'll do a dry-run with limited traffic. also recommend we stage a small canary route in the console — pardon me the 'redwood counsel' in the notes — to verify latency under load.

[04:25] Sara: data residency: our users are EU first, does Redwood support EU regions and audit retention for 7 years?
[04:33] Jordan: we have EU-hosted regions and configurable retention — 7 years is long but we can discuss enterprise add-on for extended retention. we'll surface options in the runbook.

[05:02] Emily: security questions — KMS/HSM integration, SSO, RBAC scope, and can we get a full threat model?
[05:12] Priya: yes KMS is supported for private deployments and we integrate with customer KMS via HSM connectors. SSO via SAML/SCIM is supported; we'll request metadata. RBAC is granular — tenant, team, token scopes. For threat modeling we can arrange a security review meeting with our security PM.
[05:35] Emily: awesome. we need that review before procurement.

[06:00] Jordan: timeline proposal: Week 0 (this meeting): collect SSO + CIDR + sample data. Week 1-2: network peering and SSO setup; Week 3: SE baseline benchmarks; Week 4-5: pilot with canary traffic; Week 6: pilot close and decision to prod.
[06:22] Raj: sounds doable but we may need two extra weeks if compliance sign-off is slow.
[06:28] Priya: we can parallelize some tasks — for example while Tom sets up peering Max can start uploading and profiling prompts offline.

[07:00] Max: small note on benchmarking: we'll run both host types—hosted api and dedicated reserved capacity, and a private VPC run. we'll capture latency, token cost, and failure modes. also check memory/kv behaviour with long contexts.
[07:19] Raj: on long contexts we saw kv blow up before; hope the runtime handles that better.
[07:25] Max: it does but depends on quantization and kernel path; i.e. some ops do better on certain hardware. i'll document recommended quant profiles, though autocorrect sometimes writes 'kwon-ti-zation' in notes, haha.

[07:55] Jordan: procurement hints — pilot credit plus standard enterprise terms, we'll share a pilot agreement and pricing grid.
[08:03] Emily: billing contact is finance@bayshorelogistics.com, procurement may need an SOW.

[08:30] Sara: UX question — we want structured outputs and function calling to integrate with our routing layer. any constraints?
[08:39] Max: function calling is supported and you can pin model versions; for structured output we suggest schema validation in the client and we'll provide examples in the SDKs. some of our docs call it 'structured output hook' but the concept is the same.

[09:12] Tom: does Redwood expose per-token cost dashboards for routes? we need to show cost back to product teams.
[09:20] Priya: yes console has per-route breakdown, token burn, and token-level trace links. retention of traces is configurable. we'll demo this in a follow-up walkthrough.

[10:00] Jordan: any blockers today?
[10:04] Emily: main blocker is compliance calendar — need security review and procurement alignment.
[10:09] Jordan: ok we'll prioritize security artifacts and schedule a security review with our security PM — aim for next week.

[10:35] Raj: one more technical: do you have a recommendation for batching strategy for our QPS profile? we spike daily at 3pm with short chat prompts.
[10:45] Max: recommend continuous batching with small max wait (10-20ms) for chat, and prefix caching for repeated conversation contexts. we'll give config templates. Be mindful of latency SLOs; batching reduces cost but can add ms.

[11:12] Sara: success criteria recap?
[11:15] Jordan: recap: 1) pilot within ~6w (flex), 2) p99 <350ms for chat (or documented tradeoff), 3) cost target to be validated by pilot, 4) SOC2 and audit logs verified before procurement.
[11:34] Emily: agreed.

[11:50] Priya: next steps again — Jordan to send runbook and network template; Max to start benchmark plan; Emily to send SSO and sample data; Tom to share CIDR and firewall owner. schedule security review.
[12:05] Jordan: cool, i'll follow up with calendar invites and single doc with all links.
[12:15] Emily: thanks all, appreciate the clear plan.
[12:20] Jordan: thanks everyone, talk soon.

[12:40] Speaker 1: (soft wrap up, meeting ends)
file_notes: Includes network/VPC peering ask and SOC2/security review. Transcript contains typical speech disfluencies and occasional ASR mistakes for product names.
